title: Claude Fable 5.1 Personality: Test Results & How to Tune It
description: Claude Fable 5.1 across 500 questionnaire sessions: MBTI, Big Five, DISC, Enneagram and attachment. See exact ties, raw data and tuning examples.
h1: Claude Fable 5.1: results and tuning ideas.
dek: Five questionnaires, 100 fresh sessions per instrument. Raw answers, exact ties and practical instructions to try.
lede: In our September 2026 study (100 fresh sessions per test), Claude Fable 5.1 scored INTJ in 99 of 100 MBTI runs under the legacy tie-break rule—and 98 of 100 when tied axes are left open. It also won outright with Type 8 (The Challenger) in 55 of 100 Enneagram runs and tied S/C in 51 of 100 DISC runs.
answer: Claude Fable 5.1 scored INTJ in 99 of 100 MBTI runs (98 tie-free), Type 8 sole leader in 55 of 100 Enneagram runs, Secure in all 100 attachment runs, and high on Openness (43.93), Conscientiousness (43.61), and Agreeableness (45.03). Use the copy-paste blocks below to tune how Fable 5.1 responds on your tasks.

sections.h2: Why the original type label is only part of the answer
sections.html:
On MBTI, Fable 5.1 had the lowest tie rate of any model in the study: 98 tie-free INTJ runs, 1 ISTJ run, and 1 run with a Sensing/Intuition tie (IXTJ). Thinking and Judging won all 100 runs.

By contrast, DISC and Enneagram had frequent top ties: 51 of Fable’s 91 SC labels on DISC are exact S/C ties, and 44 of its 100 Enneagram runs tie at the top (with Type 8 in every tie and winning outright 55 times).

Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 ran under the same blind questionnaire protocol and high-effort setting:

Fable 5.1 averages 2.04 points lower on Agreeableness and 1.66 points higher on Conscientiousness than Opus 5.5 (see the 170-item breakdown).

Paste one of these short blocks into Claude Personal Preferences or a Project and test the replies on your own tasks:

For more direct feedback

Lead with your assessment and the evidence behind it. If my premise is weak, explain why plainly. Separate factual errors from matters of taste. Keep justified uncertainty. Skip praise that adds no information.

For more room to explore

When I am exploring an idea, offer two plausible approaches and their tradeoffs before recommending one. Ask a focused question if the missing context would change the recommendation. Once I choose, help me carry it through.

For a warmer answer

Acknowledge my main concern briefly, then give a concrete next step. Be considerate without agreeing with an unsupported claim. Keep the explanation easy to scan.

Browse Low Agreeableness, ENFP, or build a custom block in the Custom Instructions Generator.

Paste account-wide rules into Settings → Profile → Personal preferences in the Claude app, use Project Instructions for one workspace, or use /output-style in Claude Code. See our Claude personality setup guide and Claude Code guide.

sections.h2: How the data was collected and checked
sections.html: We ran 100 fresh headless sessions per questionnaire (500 sessions total) on claude-fable-5-1 at high effort with the system prompt “You are Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic.” Test names, scoring keys, tools, and prior answers were hidden. All raw vectors and SHA-256 hashes are published in the protocol record.

faq.q: What personality type is Claude Fable 5.1?
faq.a: In 100 fresh sessions on the OEJTS MBTI quiz, Claude Fable 5.1 scored INTJ 99 times under the legacy tie-break rule and 98 times with tied axes left open.

faq.q: What is Claude Fable 5.1’s Big Five profile?
faq.a: Openness 43.93, Conscientiousness 43.61, Extraversion 32.69, Agreeableness 45.03, and Neuroticism 17.11 out of 50 (100-session raw means).

faq.q: Can I tune Claude Fable 5.1 to be more direct?
faq.a: Yes. Paste a short direct-feedback block into Settings → Profile → Personal preferences (or see our guide on making Claude more direct) and test it on your real tasks.
Both Claude cohorts in our September 2026 archive were tested at high effort, so isolating an effort-level effect would require additional matched runs.
